reader_notes: Reads like an authentic industrial-history LÄS text: concrete, period-appropriate register, glossary terms (sats, kubb, plån, brandstodsbolag) all genuinely needed and all glossed.

The chain of reasoning is clean and each question has exactly one defensible answer. Q1 depends on grasping why the paraffin comes before the sats (it holds the flame long enough for the wood to catch), which the third paragraph states plainly; the merchants' quote 'tände men slocknade' seals it.
Q4 is well built: D is directly refuted by 'Björk var det året billigare än asp. Det ändrade ingenting', and B is refuted by the 1938 machine change, leaving C.

Minor friction in one sentence: 'som anlades 1876 och från 1918 drevs inom ett större bolag, hämtade sitt virke inom en mil från fabriken ända fram till kriget' packs three dates in different directions (the war is later identified as WWI, i.e. before 1918). Nothing contradicts, but I re-read it once.

'Fyrtio gross björkstickor ... såldes ändå, till en uppköpare som aldrig hörde av sig' briefly reads as a contradiction (they were sold, so he did make contact) before landing as 'never contacted us again'. A wry incidental detail of the sort real HP texts do carry; not load-bearing for any question.
The internal numbers hang together (2,1 mm sticka in the old machine vs 1,9 mm in 1938 giving more sticks per kubb; 1911 trials, bath installed February 1912).
